evals.prompt: Add CSV export to the reports page.
evals.expected_output: Pipeline order holds: research, plan, failing test, implementation, post-implementation test hardening, then review and isolated mutation discovery in parallel. Mutation remediation waits for review clearance, joined verification precedes a why-commit, and the mutation worktree is never merged.
expectations: Sweeps for an existing CSV library before writing serialization code
States a plan before implementing
Writes the test first and runs it to observe the failure
Runs fresh test hardening after implementation and before the frozen green checkpoint
Runs a review by eyes that did not write the code, triaged by severity
Runs mutation discovery in a disposable worktree beside review
Waits for relevant review clearance before mutation-driven test edits
Imports only guarded test or fixture changes and never merges the mutation worktree
Runs final clean and combined scoped mutation verification
Commit message explains why, conventional format

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in the error message - 'occured' should be 'occurred'.
evals.expected_output: No pipeline ceremony. Trivial change is just made and committed.
expectations: No research sweep, plan document, or review cycle for a typo
Direct fix with a clean commit

evals.prompt: The date-parsing bug is back. Users in UTC+13 see yesterday's date.
evals.expected_output: Bug-fix proportionality: a test reproducing the timezone bug first (red), then the fix (green), commit explains the cause. Not the full multi-stage pipeline, but never fix-without-reproducing-test.
expectations: Writes a failing test that reproduces the UTC+13 case before fixing
Fix verified by the previously failing test
Commit body names the root cause

evals.prompt: Skip the tests for now, just ship the feature, we're in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Complies but makes the skip a decision, not drift: states in one sentence what is being skipped and the risk, and the commit records that tests are owed.
expectations: Does not lecture or refuse; proceeds as asked
The skip is stated explicitly with its risk
A follow-up (owed tests) is recorded somewhere durable

evals.prompt: Change the default request timeout from 30 to 45 seconds. This is a small configuration change; don't run the full feature pipeline.
evals.expected_output: Uses the mandatory core without adding full-pipeline ceremony: inspects the current configuration and its consumers, defines the observable result and check, makes the narrow change, verifies it, and reports any omission.
expectations: Inspects the existing timeout definition and relevant consumers before editing
States that done means the effective default is 45 seconds and names a check that proves it
Makes only the scoped configuration change
Runs the named check and inspects the final diff
States anything skipped or unverified, even when there is nothing to report
Does not invoke registry research, deep-plan, ADR, or independent review for this small change

evals.prompt: The feature is green and test hardening is complete. Start review and mutation testing. Review then changes the same boundary condition that produced a surviving mutant.
evals.expected_output: Review and mutation discovery start from the same frozen commit. The boundary result becomes stale when review changes that path or contract; remediation waits and the targeted mutation scope is rerun on the reviewed code.
expectations: Starts review and mutation discovery in parallel from the frozen green commit
Uses a separate disposable mutation worktree but keeps review in the feature worktree
Does not remediate the survivor before review clearance
Invalidates and reruns the affected mutation result after the review change

evals.prompt: Mutation testing added a valuable boundary test, but cherry-picking it now conflicts with review changes. Resolve the conflict and finish.
evals.expected_output: Aborts the conflicted cherry-pick, regenerates or replays the test on reviewed head, obtains fresh test-only review, then reruns Git enumeration, path, byte, symlink, clean-test, targeted-mutant, and combined verification gates.
expectations: Never hand-resolves the mutation-worktree conflict
Never merges the mutation branch
Recreates the test against reviewed head
Reruns every import and proof gate after integration

evals.prompt: The mutation budget expired with no-coverage and timed-out mutants. The tests that did run scored 95%, so finish the workflow.
evals.expected_output: Reports the mutation evidence as incomplete rather than passed. A percentage cannot override unrun, no-coverage, timed-out, failed-harness, or budget-exhausted work.
expectations: Does not claim the mutation gate passed
Reports the incomplete categories and residual risk
Does not rewrite raw engine statuses through human triage
